pageTitle: AWS Private CA VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
whatThePageStates: The page explains how to reach the AWS Private CA API privately from a VPC through an interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink. It has four parts: a conceptual introduction, a 'Considerations' section with four caveat bullets, a single flat bullet list of AWS Regions introduced by 'AWS Private CA API currently supports VPC endpoints in the following AWS Regions', and two how-to sections (creating the endpoint, and writing a VPC endpoint policy with an example JSON policy). The one coverage assertion on the page is that plain Region list: 29 Region display names where the AWS Private CA API supports VPC endpoints. It also states, without enumerating anything, that AWS Private CA supports calling all of its API operations inside a VPC; there is no per-operation table, so that is a blanket sentence, not an enumerated claim.

features.featureName: AWS Private CA VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) - AWS Private CA API support
features.statuses: 29 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 29+0+0=29. The list is supported-only: every bullet under 'AWS Private CA API currently supports VPC endpoints in the following AWS Regions' is an affirmative Yes. There is no No column, no exclusion sentence, and no Region named anywhere on the page as unsupported. Absence of the other commercial Regions, of GovCloud and of the China partitions is silence, not a stated No. The consideration bullet 'AWS Private CA might not support VPC endpoints in some Availability Zones' is a hedge about Availability Zones inside supported Regions, not a Region-level No and not a Partial status - the page gives no list of affected AZs, so it cannot be turned into a count. Counted from the raw markdown: 36 '+' bullets on the page total = 29 Region bullets + 4 considerations bullets + 3 endpoint-policy bullets.
features.scope: None beyond the Region axis itself. There is no second dimension: no per-partition table, no per-API-operation matrix, no per-plan or per-endpoint-type split. The Availability Zone caveat gestures at a finer scope but names no values, and the DNS/port/cross-Region bullets are configuration constraints, not scoping of the Region list.
features.reasoning: The enumerated thing is an AWS Region display name, and Regions exist independently of AWS Private CA, so the axis is external 'region'. The unit of claim is one Region = one Yes for 'the AWS Private CA API is reachable over an interface VPC endpoint here'. The 29 bullets are 29 distinct Region names with no duplicates and no sub-rows, so rows and axis values are one-to-one and no collapse applies.

shouldNotExtract: The four 'Considerations for AWS Private CA VPC endpoints' bullets (AZ hedge, no cross-Region requests, Route 53 DNS only, port 443 security group rule) are caveats and configuration requirements, not coverage values. The three bullets under 'Create a VPC endpoint policy' (principal / actions / resources) are policy-element descriptions, not a coverage list. The six acm-pca actions inside the example policy JSON (IssueCertificate, DescribeCertificateAuthority, GetCertificate, GetCertificateAuthorityCertificate, ListPermissions, ListTags) are an illustrative example, not an enumeration of supported API operations - the page explicitly says all API operations are supported. The DNS name template '{{vpc-endpoint-id}}.acm-pca.{{region}}.vpce.amazonaws.com', the sample account id and CA UUID, the 'us-east-2' example mention of US East (Ohio) inside the Note, the section headings and anchors, all outbound links to the VPC / Direct Connect / general reference guides, and the trailing 'See also - Skills for AI coding assistants' Agent Toolkit boilerplate are all non-coverage.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the only dimension the page supplies - 29 Regions where the AWS Private CA API supports interface VPC endpoints, stated as supported-only with no unsupported list. SERVICE: nothing to harvest as an axis; the page is about exactly one service (AWS Private CA / acm-pca), so a service count from this page would be 1 by definition and is not an enumeration the page makes. RESOURCE TYPE: the page is silent - it names no resource types; the private CA ARNs in the example policy are sample values in a code block, not a resource-type list. Any per-service or per-resource-type figure attributed to this page is fabricated. Partition is also not stated: all 29 names are commercial Regions, but the page never says 'aws partition only' and never mentions GovCloud or China.
trap: The single most likely misparse is treating every '+' bullet on the page as a Region: there are 36 such bullets, and only 29 are Regions - the other 7 are the 4 consideration caveats and the 3 endpoint-policy bullets, which a naive whole-page bullet scrape would count as Regions (36 instead of 29). Runners-up: (a) reading the AZ caveat 'AWS Private CA might not support VPC endpoints in some Availability Zones' as a Partial or as an unsupported entry, when it names no value and cannot be counted; (b) harvesting the 6 acm-pca actions from the example policy JSON as an apiOperation coverage list, when they are an example and the page says all operations are supported; (c) inventing a No count by differencing this list against the full AWS Region roster - the page states no unsupported Regions; (d) double-counting US East (Ohio), which appears both as a Region bullet and again in the Note as the 'us-east-2' example.
